title: Discrete modules with continuous group action form an abelian category with enough injectives
statement: Let $G$ be a profinite group and $A$ a finite ring. Let $\mathcal C$ have as objects left $A$-modules $M$ with an action of $G$ by $A$-linear automorphisms for which the stabilizer of every $m\in M$ is open, and as morphisms the $A$-linear $G$-equivariant maps. Then $\mathcal C$ is an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] with enough injective objects [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Kernels and cokernels are the corresponding $A$-module kernels and cokernels with their induced $G$-actions; a sequence in $\mathcal C$ is exact precisely when its underlying sequence of $A$-modules is exact.

external.place: Tag 04JF, label lemma-G-modules (functorial injective embeddings in Mod_{R,G})

proof.text: For a morphism of discrete $A$-modules with continuous $G$-action, the underlying module kernel is stable under the action, and every element of it has the same open stabilizer as in the source. The underlying cokernel inherits the action; the stabilizer of a quotient class contains the open stabilizer of any representative, so it is open. Thus the zero object, finite biproducts, kernels, and cokernels are those in the underlying module category, and exactness is detected on underlying $A$-modules. The normal-kernel and conormal-cokernel conditions for monomorphisms and epimorphisms are the corresponding module conditions. Therefore the structural criterion in [def-sp-abelian] makes $\mathcal C$ an abelian category.

source.place: Tag 0A2H, label section-group-cohomology: open stabilizers and the R-G-module category; the kernel/cokernel verification is the direct module-category construction

proof.text: By the functorial injective-embedding result for $R$-$G$-modules [lem-exc-discrete-modules-abelian-injective-embeddings], specialized to the discrete-action subcategory, every object of $\mathcal C$ admits a monomorphism into an injective object. Hence $\mathcal C$ has enough injectives in the sense of [def-sp-injective-resolutions].
